label: Upwork
terms_note: Upwork's User Agreement and API Terms of Use ban automated access to a freelancer account and automated proposal submission — the GraphQL API exposes no proposal mutation and a key is granted to the account holder, never to a platform. Registering, editing the profile or submitting a proposal through a browser session is automation those terms forbid; the tenant opts in per account, and Upwork's usual enforcement is a suspended or closed account.

discovery.auth: oauth2 (API key applied for per organization; Upwork approves)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **partial** (GraphQL API — job search, contracts, milestones, messaging; no proposal submission documented). Lane `assist` → **api for search + status** after key approval; proposals assist. Confidence high (docs + terms read via r.jina.ai).
auth: 1. Apply for an API key at upwork.com/developer/keys/apply (organization context, intended use, 40k/day confirmation) → Upwork approval → OAuth2 authorization code → access token.
reference.limits: - 300 req/min/IP, 40,000/day; webhooks subscriptions need Upwork approval; ToS: no robots/scrapers without written permission, no proposal spam.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: Client ID of an approved Upwork API key (apply at https://www.upwork.com/developer/keys/apply; Upwork reviews every key).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: Client secret of the same API key (form body of the refresh_token grant).

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token from the Authorization Code Grant for the freelancer/agency account; the runtime mints access tokens (TTL 86400 s) at https://www.upwork.com/api/v3/oauth2/token and keeps the rotated refresh_token each response returns (set PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR to persist it).

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.help: Optional organization id sent as X-Upwork-API-TenantId (the execution context; without it the user's default organization is used).

adapter.rate_note: 'We allow 300 requests per minute per IP address … HTTP 429' and the key application confirms staying within 40,000 requests per day; caching beyond 24 hours is not allowed. Two requests per second.
adapter.terms: Upwork API Terms of Use (https://www.upwork.com/legal#api): no robots or scrapers without written permission, no proposal spam, no caching for more than 24 hours; every key is approved by Upwork for a declared use.

me.note: POST /graphql query { user { id nid rid } } — the authenticated user (account.data.user).

body.query: =query SearchJobs($filter: MarketplaceJobPostingsSearchFilter) { marketplaceJobPostingsSearch(marketPlaceJobFilter: $filter, searchType: USER_JOBS_SEARCH, sortAttributes: [{ field: RECENCY }]) { totalCount edges { node { id title description ciphertext publishedDateTime createdDateTime amount { rawValue currency displayValue } hourlyBudgetMin { rawValue currency } hourlyBudgetMax { rawValue currency } skills { name } category subcategory totalApplicants client { totalFeedback } } } pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage } } }

search_postings.note: POST https://api.upwork.com/graphql marketplaceJobPostingsSearch (permission 'Read marketplace Job Postings'), searchType USER_JOBS_SEARCH, newest first (sortAttributes RECENCY), following the documented real-life example. `query` → searchExpression_eq (partial Lucene syntax); `category` → categoryIds_any[0] (an Upwork category id); `min_budget` → budgetRange_eq.rangeStart (whole number; hourly jobs are returned regardless of budget); page/limit → pagination_eq {after: offset as a string, as in the example's "0", first: limit}. Money values are strings (amount.rawValue / displayValue, hourlyBudgetMin/Max) and skills are {name} objects, so they stay in raw; the job page is https://www.upwork.com/jobs/~<raw.node.ciphertext>. GraphQL failures arrive as HTTP 200 with errors[]: a null data is reported as an error, but a permission error on the field alone yields an empty list.

body.query: =query JobDetails($id: ID!) { marketplaceJobPosting(id: $id) { id content { title description } contractTerms { contractType } clientCompanyPublic { id } } }

get_posting.note: POST /graphql marketplaceJobPosting(id) with the documented fields (content.title/description, contractTerms.contractType, clientCompanyPublic.id in raw). id is the job posting id (the search result id).

body.query: =query Proposal($id: ID!) { vendorProposal(id: $id) { id status { status } viewedByClient } }

bid_status.note: POST /graphql vendorProposal(id) → status.status (VendorProposalStatusName: Accepted, Declined, Withdrawn, Offered, Activated, Archived, Hired, Pending); viewedByClient in raw. For freelancers/agencies (permission 'Client Proposals - Read And Write Access'); the agency context follows X-Upwork-API-TenantId.

body.query: =query RoomMessages($filter: RoomStoryFilter!) { roomStories(filter: $filter) { edges { node { id message createdDateTime user { id name } } } } }

list_messages.note: POST /graphql roomStories(filter: {roomId_eq, storyFilter.pagination {after: "", first}}) as in the documented example. thread_id is the room id (e.g. room_d4ad…) and is required by the API. Only the first `limit` stories are returned (cursor paging is not followed; page is ignored).

body.query: =mutation SendRoomMessage($roomId: ID!, $message: String!) { createRoomStoryV2(input: { roomId: $roomId, message: $message }) { id message } }

send_message.note: POST /graphql createRoomStoryV2(input: {roomId, message}) — posts a message into the Upwork room as the authenticated user (visible to the other party immediately).

not_offered.submit_bid: The GraphQL reference documents no mutation that submits a freelancer proposal (only clientProposals/messageClientProposal for clients and vendorProposals reads); proposals are submitted on upwork.com.
not_offered.withdraw_bid: No mutation to withdraw a vendor proposal is documented.
not_offered.credits: Connects balance is not exposed by a documented query.
